statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 14 of 100 in the low band, eleven points below the 25 block threshold, while stress is extreme at 82 and confidence high at 89.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window spans the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: NQ has eased to 29,294.00, up 0.54%, about 46 points below a 29,339.75 session high that did not extend this hour, so a retracement was granted rather than denied; VIX is 17.18, the 10-year 4.951% and WTI $99.13, leaving tail at 14 and stress extreme at 82 roughly an hour before the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report.
body:
The decisive new evidence this hour is a retracement that was granted. NQ trades 29,294.00, up 158.75 points or 0.54% against a 29,135.25 previous close, and two independent feeds agree on the price, the change and the 29,339.75 session high. An hour ago price was 29,324.75 and sat roughly fifteen points under that same high. It has since eased about thirty points and now sits some forty-six points below it, while the high itself has not advanced at all.

That matters because the amplifier cited in the previous assessment was proximity to a session extreme. Price has stepped away from the extreme rather than pressing it, and the high has failed to extend across a full hour. Repeated extension after failed retracements is the structure tail risk is built to capture, and the observed sequence is its opposite: the market gave back part of the advance without being bid straight back into the high. Tail therefore eases a point to 14, comfortably inside the low band. The advance itself is intact, with price still in the upper sixth of a 299-point range measured from the 29,040.50 overnight low, so the dominant mode remains trend-up; what has changed is the efficiency of that trend, not its direction.

Cross-asset evidence continues to withhold confirmation. VIX is 17.18, down 3.70%, inside a 17.07 to 17.71 band and only marginally off the session low set earlier. The ten-year yield is 4.951%, up under a basis point from a 4.944% previous close and sitting mid-range between 4.936% and 4.978%; the two-year is 4.560%, up about a basis point and below its 4.583% high. Both have ticked slightly higher since the previous assessment, which is a mild reversal of the earlier easing but is not the aligned, accelerating move that would matter. The thirty-year holds near 5.3565%. None of these channels is aligned with an equity melt-up.

Energy has held its correction. WTI is $99.13, down $3.37 or 3.28%, and Brent is $103.88, down 3.48%. Both remain roughly 9% higher on the week. Two developments underlie the pullback: the International Energy Agency cut its 2026 demand forecast by 2.5 million barrels a day, the steepest reduction since the pandemic, while diplomatic efforts around the Strait of Hormuz are being weighed against continued fighting. Working the other way, Houthi advances toward the Bab al-Mandeb Strait have renewed supply-route concern. The net is a meaningful reduction in the near-term inflation impulse an hour before the inflation print, inside an energy regime that remains elevated and unresolved.

Stress rises a point to 82 and stays extreme. The environment is unchanged in substance and the clock has moved closer to the release. A global bond selloff has carried the ten-year toward 5% after an eleven basis point spike on Thursday took it to its highest since October 2023, the long end is pressured by supply, crude sits above $100 on an unresolved Middle East conflict, and the three major U.S. averages fell for a fourth consecutive session on Thursday. Positioning corroborates the caution: CFTC data show speculative S&P 500 net shorts increased by 4,587 contracts to 307,558 while managers cut net longs by 19,361. This is precisely the difficult, high-volatility environment stress describes, and it is scored independently of the price-path question.

The August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC is the final inflation input before the 16 September decision, with consensus at 0.4% month-on-month and 3.4% year-on-year headline and 0.2% and 2.4% for core. It is a checkpoint, not an automatic block. Its importance and the dispersion around it are carried in stress and confidence; tail will be revised on the observed post-release path rather than on the magnitude of any surprise. The conditional forecast peaks at 23 in the release slot and 22 across the cash open, both inside the watch band and beneath the 25 block threshold, then decays through the afternoon on the assumption that retracements continue to be granted.

One sector input still supports the overnight bid. TSMC's August revenue of NT$514.81 billion, up 10.1% on the month and 53.3% on the year, is a record and a fourth consecutive monthly high, with advanced five, four and three nanometre capacity fully booked by artificial-intelligence demand. Thursday's U.S. semiconductor session was negative, so this remains a catalyst the last cash close did not fully reflect.

Confidence holds at 89. Two independent live NQ feeds agree exactly on price, change and session high; real-time VIX and two-year and ten-year yields are current; both crude benchmarks are current; and the seven-day calendar was re-verified against a primary calendar source this hour, with today's release times confirmed. Two news outlets returned bot-block responses to direct retrieval, so narrative confirmation came through alternative verified items rather than those pages. The shared cross-asset context file was both outside its ninety-minute freshness window, at roughly four hours and forty-five minutes old, and flagged as a partial collection, so it was not used; this assessment rests entirely on independently fetched live evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 11:00 UTC on 10 September to 10:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 14 with the mode recorded as trend-down through the pre-release grind. The single excursion sits in the U.S. morning: 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and the window peak of 24 at 13:00 UTC across the cash open with the mode back to trend-down. Those two slots are the only ones mapped to WATCH and neither reached the 25 block threshold. Tail then decayed as price discovery stayed orderly, easing to 17 by 14:00 UTC and holding 14 to 19 through the afternoon, with event/whipsaw recorded again at 20:00 and 21:00 UTC around the cash close. From 22:00 UTC the overnight session normalised into an 11 to 15 band with mixed conditions. The final five slots at 06:00 through 10:00 UTC record trend-up at tail 13, 14, 13, 14 and 15 as the overnight advance extended, was bought back and then stalled beneath its high. Stress never left the extreme band, running 81 to 87 across the whole window, and confidence held 85 to 89 throughout.
outlookSummary: The forward window covers the rest of the 11 September session and then ends deep inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail starts at 14 on the observed retracement away from a session high that did not extend. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report, inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, and 22 in the 13:00 UTC slot spanning the cash open where a post-event move is either confirmed by opening-auction continuation or rejected by a first genuine pullback. The 14:00 UTC slot carrying the preliminary Michigan release eases to 19 on the assumption that price discovery is orderly by then. The afternoon decays through 17, 16 and 15, holds 15 across the budget statement, lifts to 16 into the final pre-close hour and 18 across the 20:00 UTC cash close where weekly positioning concentrates, then falls to a 5 to 6 floor for the fourteen closure hours, which represents residual gap risk into the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen rather than any intraday mechanism. Two slots are mapped to WATCH and none reaches the block threshold. Stress stays extreme through the U.S. session, peaking at 92 in the release slot, and decays through elevated into moderate across the closure. Confidence eases from 89 to 62 as the horizon moves past the last observable quote.
